fields.description:
## Context
Cloud/DC atomic executors need a core route that bypasses generic retry without falsely advancing the current handler baseline. Production must remain on legacy until S3 validates and cuts over.

## Outcome
Add a constructor-injected legacy-default selector for exact summary updates, map confirmed outcomes through the existing result surface, and expose terminal outcomes as bounded per-mutation errors without baseline/provenance advance. Finalize the S1 section of ADR 0103.

## Plan
1. Route only exact `{"summary"}` when tests explicitly enable the selector. Mixed fields remain one unsplit legacy call. Add no config/env key and never dual-send.
2. Poison-test generic `_call_with_retry` on the selected route. Preserve every unselected route.
3. SUCCESS cohort. The S1 T2/T3 summary executors emit `applied` and `recovered` on success; map both to the legacy successful-update result surface (`result={"key": jira_key}`, leaving `error`/`_comment_errors`/`_subop` as legacy success does) and advance the ADR-0026 baseline. Include `already_satisfied` in the success cohort as a DEFENSIVE/forward-compat no-op mapping — it is NOT currently emitted by the S1 executors, so pin it with a test asserting it advances the baseline identically. Because `OperationOutcome` carries NO field payload, the success route derives the value written to `_fields_synced`/`ctx.synced_fields` from the routed mutation's own `fields["summary"]` (the string just sent), keyed by the mutation's `local_id`; that is what reaches the baseline advance and preserves byte-parity with the legacy `{"key": jira_key}` result surface.
4. TERMINAL cohort. Map EVERY other disposition the executors can return — `commit_unknown`, `retryable_deferred`, `permanent_failure`, `exhausted_transient`, and any further non-success disposition (`dependency_deferred`, `scope_deferred`, `safety_aborted`, `skipped`) — identically as terminal: emit an internal tagged result consumed by `handle_update` that sets `result=None`, records exactly one redacted per-mutation error/disposition message capped at 512 Unicode code points, carries the OperationOutcome `retry_not_before` value (a RetryPlan field, not a disposition) onto the manifest for observability only, keeps `_fields_synced` empty, advances no baseline/provenance, persists no S1 deferral, and continues the batch.
5. Name S3 as sole cutover, fuse/deferral consumer, and bridge-retirement owner in contract/ADR.

## Testing
Use exact-versus-mixed routing tables, poison retries, Cloud/DC verified fakes, and apply-handler spies asserting one message, redaction, the 512-code-point boundary, and the derived-from-`fields["summary"]` baseline value — across the success cohort (`applied`, `recovered`, and the defensive `already_satisfied`) and the terminal cohort (`commit_unknown`, `retryable_deferred`, and the 512/redaction boundary).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The internal selector defaults to legacy and adds no config or environment key.
- [x] Test-enabled exact summary bypasses generic retry, while mixed fields remain one legacy call.
- [x] The success dispositions `applied` and `recovered` (plus the defensive, not-currently-emitted `already_satisfied`) preserve all existing result and telemetry shapes and advance the baseline with the summary derived from the routed mutation's `fields["summary"]`.
- [x] Every non-success disposition (`commit_unknown`, `retryable_deferred`, `permanent_failure`, `exhausted_transient`, and any further terminal disposition) records exactly one redacted per-mutation error/disposition message capped at 512 Unicode code points and never advances baseline or provenance.
- [x] Terminal outcomes persist no deferral in S1 and do not stop unrelated batch work.
- [x] ADR 0103 names S3 as sole production cutover, fuse/deferral consumer, and compatibility-bridge retirement owner.

## Out of scope
Default-on routing, fuse behavior, and durable deferral remain RP-03 S3.
